facts.statement: The only known fossils of Zhylgaia are two partial humeri found in an upper Paleocene layer in Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: Its remains, consisting of two partial humeri, were recovered from an upper Paleocene deposit in Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: Zhylgaia was once placed in the artificial group Graculavidae, which included Late Cretaceous and Paleocene shorebirds that looked similar but were not closely related.
facts.quote: Zhylgaia was assigned to the form taxon "Graculavidae", an assemblage of Late Cretaceous and Paleocene shorebirds which are not a natural clade but merely an assemblage of superficially similar birds.

facts.statement: In 2008, researchers reclassified Zhylgaia into the family Prophaethontidae because its anatomy and size matched the extinct tropicbird-like Lithoptila.
facts.quote: In 2008, Zhylgaia was assigned to Prophaethontidae—an extinct family related to modern tropicbirds—on the basis of its anatomy and size closely matching the prophaethontid Lithoptila.

facts.statement: Zhylgaia lived during the Thanetian stage of the Paleocene, between 59.24 and 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Thanetian to Thanetian (59.24 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: Zhylgaia is considered a modern bird, likely belonging to the Neognathae group.
facts.quote: All that can be said about this taxon is that it was a modern bird, most likely a neognath.
